topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing and overview of learning outcomes for the lecture series.

topics.label: Cancer development as a failure of differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the foundational concept of cancer as a multistep process driven by genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt normal cellular differentiation, tissue architecture, and cell culture modeling.

topics.label: Distinction, invasion, and stepwise progression of benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the histological and clinical differences between benign and malignant tumors, focusing on tissue invasion, metastatic spread, and the stepwise progression from precursor lesions.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification conventions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and exceptions used to name benign and malignant tumors based on their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the pathophysiological processes through which primary and metastatic tumors cause clinical illness and patient death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence across human populations and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the epidemiology and patterns of tumor occurrence across human populations and diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Cancer screening principles and clinical detection methods
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical rationale, histological indicators, and practical challenges of population screening for various cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing, summarizing the session and giving instructions for upcoming practicals.
